newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Yankee issue seen as vote of confidence.
newsitem.headline: S.African Yankee issue seen as vote of confidence.

text.p: The pricing and maturity of South Africa's second Yankee bond issue underscored improving foreign investor confidence in the country, analysts said on Thursday.
Lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co Inc announced earlier that South Africa had raised $500 million over 20 years at a 183 basis point spread above similar dated U.S. Treasuries.
Analysts said the latest issue compared favourably with earlier ones.
In October last year, South Africa's first Yankee issue came in at a 195-point spread over 10 years, while in January the 10-year sterling issue carried a 190-point spread.
South Africa's first global dollar issue in December 1994, which carried a five-year maturity, had a 193-point spread.
"This issue is very competitively priced," said Tertia Jacobs, gilts analyst at SocGen Frankel Pollak.
"The critical thing is that they have lengthened their maturity profile which creates a better environment for parastatals to borrow offshore."
"It is also a vote of confidence that they have managed to succeed in doing it at such a competitive spread," Jacobs said.
Mike Lamont, director fixed interest at Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank, said the fact that the spread had come in below market expectations was also positive.
"I think since foreigners were giving it a bit of a higher spread...most people were expecting 190 to 210...the fact that it came out lower is very good news and a sign of confidence," Lamont said.
Rand Merchant Bank Treasury economist Julia Roy said the better pricing for the bonds, which are issued in the United States, also reflected South Africa's improving investment ratings.

Last week U.S. rating agency Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said it had assigned an investment grade BBB minus rating to the country's foreign currency debt, matching the assessment of Moody's Investors Service Inc.

Analysts expect Standard and Poor's Corp to follow suit when it reviews its rating later this year. S&P currently rates South African long-term foreign currency debt at BB plus -- one notch below investment grade.

UAL Merchant Bank Treasury senior general manager Peter Lane said the issue should have positive implications for the bond market, but that looming foreign exchange controls relaxations on July 1 currently held sway over sentiment.
"The interpretation is that it's a positive step, but July 1 is still putting the wind up the market. Nobody wants to commit themselves until they see what the flows are like," Lane said.
Jacobs added other implications for the local bond market were that South African bonds were becoming more familiar internationally and that there was still offshore demand for high yielding bonds.
In early afternoon trade, the government's benchmark R150 rand bond was pegged at a 14.74 percent yield, having retraced from a high of 14.87 percent registered at the opening of Thursday trade.
